correctness.rationale: All 83,825,280 rank-seven maps are enumerated in two independently organized exact C++ implementations: full base-nine map tables with five-distance orbit closure and independent kernel-partition generation with full 36-pair reverse closure. Both find exactly 36,936 nonsynchronizing, zero primitive nonsynchronizing, and identical splits 1,944 / 34,992. A separate modular function count yields 36,936. Complete subset-vs-pair crosschecks at smaller state counts and sample checks at nine states support the key quotient lemma. Elementary subgroup and orbit arguments give the congruence and rotation conclusions. No finite sample is used as an infinite proof.

evidence: The 2015 primitive permutation-group theorem concerns a primitive permutation group. The fixed nine-cycle alone is imprimitive; monoid primitivity is a different hypothesis.

value.rationale: Nine is the first odd composite cyclic state count with a nontrivial proper quotient; complete classification of every rank-seven companion letter proves that congruence, and only congruence, blocks synchronization. This resolves a natural primitive-versus-synchronizing finite test beyond almost-injective special cases, with exact independently checked counts and a reusable 36-state pair-graph benchmark. It is more than a routine instance of a known table or a tiny numerical improvement.
